Incorporating the July 2021 Senior Loan Officer Opinion Survey (SLOOS) into the read of the September 22, 2021 FOMC statement:

- Credit supply and demand: Banks reported stronger demand for C&I loans across large, middle-market, and small firms, along with higher borrower inquiries; many banks eased terms on C&I loans. Foreign banks also reported stronger C&I demand tied to financing needs for inventories, accounts receivable, capex, and M&A.
- Consumer credit: Banks eased standards for consumer loans (including credit cards, auto, and other consumer credit), indicating broader household credit availability relative to 2020 and moving closer to (or easier than) 2019 in some categories.
- Banks’ rationale: Easing was cited in connection with an improved economic outlook, competition, greater risk tolerance, robust liquidity, and solid capital positions.
- Implications for the FOMC statement: SLOOS corroborates the Committee’s view that financial conditions remain accommodative and supports a constructive outlook on activity and employment. The observed strengthening in credit demand and easing in standards also aligns with the Fed’s taper signal (“may soon be warranted”) by indicating underlying momentum. Balanced against the Financial Stability Report’s flags on elevated valuations and structural funding vulnerabilities, the SLOOS nudges the tone modestly more positive while still warranting vigilance.

Net effect: Constructive with a slightly firmer growth/credit impulse than suggested by the FSR alone.
